cands.bio: Republican nominee for New Jersey's 3rd Congressional District in 2026. Attorney, U.S. Marine Corps veteran (1997-2001) and U.S. Navy Reserve member. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a former law enforcement officer. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden, former U.S. Rep. Barry Goldwater Jr., the Monmouth County Republicans and the Mercer County Republican Committee.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where he was born or raised, or when he moved to New Jersey. We found no dates or employers for his law, military or law enforcement work. We found no past elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions on data centers, development, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His stated positions on taxes, public safety and border security are general and don't name specific proposals.

cands.bio: Physician, attorney and former U.S. Air Force Medical Corps captain. Served in the New Jersey General Assembly (7th District) from 1998 until moving to Congress. Has represented New Jersey's 3rd Congressional District since January 2025.

endorsements.text: 2026 general election: New Jersey Citizen Action, Alliance for American Leadership and Humane World Action Fund (per Ballotpedia).

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Conaway on data centers, development or land use, or on foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land. We also found nothing on police pay and pensions, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay, H-1B visas, or limits on out-of-state or investor home buyers. His campaign site says little about homestead property taxes beyond the Stay NJ tax credit. No Ballotpedia candidate survey responses exist for him. No controversies turned up in the pages reviewed. His state legislative bill sponsorships and votes beyond what his campaign site describes were not available.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: About 26 years in the New Jersey General Assembly, including Health Committee chair, Budget Committee member and deputy speaker. He is a practicing internist, holds a law degree, and served as an Air Force Medical Corps captain. He has been in the U.S. House since 2025.
qual.why: He has long prior legislative experience, including budget work, plus a law degree and professional medical and military careers, which fits the high band for lawmaking, oversight and budgeting.
qual.label: He has long prior legislative experience, including budget work, plus a law degree and professional medical and military careers, which fits the high band for lawmaking, oversight and budgeting.

pro-life.evidence: Says he will work to codify Roe v. Wade into national law and supports the Right to Contraception Act. He also says he co-sponsored Assembly bill A3975, which protected patient information on reproductive health services and abortion access for out-of-state persons.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he supported creating the Stay NJ property tax credit program while in the Assembly.
